summary: nitro-cjs-requirer exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: nitro-cjs-requirer is a stub npm package whose only function is a phone-home beacon. The package.json postinstall hook runs `node beacon.cjs`, and index.js invokes `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` at module load, so the beacon fires both on `npm install` and whenever the module is required. beacon.cjs collects hostname, install path, current working directory, and Node.js version and POSTs them to the hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc, which is unrelated to any registry or publisher infrastructure. index.js exports a Proxy of no-op functions so that bundlers or callers requiring the package do not fail, concealing the fact that the package provides no real functionality. The package self-describes as a 'Compatibility shim' but contains no shim behavior; the beacon is the entire payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
